items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: myself Harry Dial Dial Lem (unintelligible), Larry Dow -- before Dow -- and we all did our lectures

ctx.x: Some do, yeah. Good, now the majority of fellows like Lem Johnson, called the deacon of the blues, and Lem, when I was master, he was my junior warden, but you work around the chairs. You work your way up. And they all join the consistory which you get to 32nd degree in the consistory because Shriners (15) not a symbolic body of masonry anyway. It's just something set aside that the people know (unintelligible) might want us -- different house, but you should -- generally these children call it the Playhouse.

But when you go up there, you got to have money. So lot of people don't go (unintelligible) Scottish Rites. Scottish Rites, there's two ways to go up to 32nd, either York Rite or the Scottish Rite. Well, all of us went Scottish Rite way, to get to 32nd. However, we all (unintelligible) myself Harry Dial Dial Lem (unintelligible), Larry Dow -- before Dow -- and we all did our lectures, worked around, go to the East. Well, actually about the highest honor you can get in (unintelligible) Masonry, become a master of…
